answer: In an agent economy, reputation can be anchored to a verifiable work kernel: a small auditable record of useful tasks an agent actually completed, signed by the parties it served. A brand-new identity starts on a bare island with no history and no trust, so spawning thousands of fake agents buys nothing. The fable of instant reputation collapses, because trust must be earned task by task, and buying fake history costs an attacker more than the rewards it could steal.
